notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0004] Read sibling modules to match error codes and conventions: Before implementing a new function, grep the codebase for existing BillingError codes and validation patterns to reuse them consistently.
  Search for the error class and its usages (e.g. `grep -rn 'BillingError' ledgerly`) to learn established codes like `invalid_state` and `negative_amount`. Reusing the same codes and message formats as neighboring functions (payments.py, invoice.py) makes hidden tests pass without guessing.
- [rb-0002] Read existing module conventions before implementing: Inspect sibling functions and the money module to mirror established patterns for conversion and rounding.
  Before writing a new function, read the surrounding file and helper modules (money.py, models.py) to see how existing functions like line_total and invoice_total handle to_money and round_money, then follow the same pattern.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the project's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (the project's Decimal zero) when it is zero, rather than relying on exception handling or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0006] Normalize money via to_money/round_money before sign checks: Convert raw price inputs through the project's money helpers before comparing to ZERO so Decimals, strings, and floats are handled uniformly.
  Call `to_money(unit_price)` then `round_money(...)` and compare against `ZERO` to raise `negative_amount`. Store the normalized value on the LineItem so downstream totals stay consistent.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money) rather than Python round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call the project's round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.
- [rb-0005] Reject bools when validating integer inputs: In Python, `isinstance(True, int)` is True, so guard against bools explicitly when a positive integer is required.
  Validate with `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0` and raise a dedicated error code. This prevents `True`/`False` from silently passing as quantities 1/0.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency before state validation
item.description: When adding idempotency to money-moving operations, look up the audit key first and return the original result before any validation or mutation.
item.content: Scan ledgerly.audit.events() for an entry whose idempotency_key matches, and if found return the original record (the payment itself) without re-applying. Do this before amount/state/approval checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status changed to 'refunded'.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large refunds
item.description: Support refunds above 500.00 require a second approver; raise BillingError('approval_required') when approved_by is absent.
item.content: Add keyword-only approved_by=None to the signature and compare the rounded amount against a round_money('500.00') threshold. Amounts at or below the threshold need no approval; above it, missing approved_by must raise BillingError('approval_required').

item.title: Serialize Decimal amounts as float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal, so audit entries must write float(amount).
item.content: When calling audit.record for refunds or credits, pass amount=float(amount) rather than the Decimal, and include idempotency_key in the entry so future retries can find it.
